scope.question: Does multi-stage real Unity maze authoring and gameplay validation amortize Splinter's preparation/completion costs versus parallel code work with one sequential Editor?
methods: Splinter independent A/B Editors with parallel checkpoint --release
Two code worktrees with one shared original Editor and alternating A/B leases
scope.input: Same committed real 2.80GB Unity project and identical current Library before both runs; frozen product 07bc2de
a: Implement and compile seeded 15x15 perfect-maze generator; validate graph
Implement authoring; generate, save and reopen three maze scenes
Improve farthest-goal selection and wall height; regenerate and verify persistence
b: Implement and compile CharacterController, InputSystem keyboard and stage state machine
Save prefab/sandbox; Play validation of keyboard movement, collision, entry and clear
Add restart and second stage; compile, save and repeat Play validation
scope.integration: Combine B into prepared A/original Editor, compile, save three playable integrated maze scenes, physically follow solution routes, validate clear/restart, render preview
scope.timing: Source code authored once by parallel agents; same cumulative source snapshots replayed in both methods. AI implementation and benchmark harness development recorded separately, not claimed as per-method elapsed time. No artificial task delay.
acceptance: Actual fresh compilation response and Editor path/PID identity
Saved/reopened layouts, scenes, GUIDs and references
Real Play Mode with public virtual keyboard event injection, CharacterController motion and physical triggers
Independent durable source results, normal shutdown, reclamation and original source restoration
scope.bounds: One successful cohort per method after any explicitly retained diagnostic failures; no service/global/package configuration edits, no game build or broad compatibility matrix. Original Library transition uses previously authorized exact lifecycle. No forced Editor exit.
